accessibilityTree.name: Nivlo stays at the edge of your screen after startup, ready to catch ideas and to-dos.
Match the system, or fix it to light / dark.
When on, the floating badge always stays above other windows.
Press it in any app to jot down a to-do right away.
Press it in any app to pop up search and jump straight to a to-do, note or tip.
Creates the search box in the background after start-up so the first press of the shortcut opens it faster (about 0.3 s → 0.12 s), at the cost of roughly 90 MB of extra memory.
No reminders pop up while paused; due reminders aren't lost — you'll get a summary when you resume. The tray menu has this switch too.
See the basics of Nivlo again.
The “Later” buttons on the badge and in the Inbox schedule items for this day.
Hide to-dos you finished today from the Today list and the floating panel.
Affects the calendar's week and month views.
Updates are signed. Your data is backed up automatically before an update is installed.
Bundles the runtime environment and recent logs (with content and tokens removed) into one archive to attach when reporting a problem. Your notes, to-dos, clipboard and files are not included.
Exports plain files any editor can open, including source information. Items in the trash are not exported.
Bundles all your data (including workflows and settings) and pasted images into one archive. Your original files and any secrets are not included.
Choose a backup archive. Your current data is backed up automatically first; the restore takes effect after a restart, and the replaced data stays in the data folder.
